title: ECHO: A Participatory Framework for Bias-Anchored AI Harm Anticipation
abstract: arXiv:2512.03068v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems increasingly shape consequential decisions, creating value but also potential harms for individuals, social groups, and society. This has prompted calls for proactive approaches that anticipate harms early in the AI lifecycle. Although prior research identifies AI biases as sources of harm, the associations between particular lifecycle biases and harms remain insufficiently understood. We introduce \texttt{ECHO}, a systematic, context-sensitive, and participatory framework that anchors early harm anticipation in lifecycle biases and elicits their perceived associations with potential harms.\texttt{ECHO} identifies domain-specific stakeholders, instantiates biases through vignettes, collects harm judgements from human participants and a large language model (LLM), and organises them into descriptive and inferential ethical matrices. translated_title: ECHO：一个以偏见为锚点的AI危害预判参与式框架
translated_abstract: 人工智能系统日益深刻地影响着各类重大决策，在创造价值的同时，也可能给个人、社会群体乃至整个社会带来潜在危害。这促使人们呼吁采取主动的方法，在人工智能生命周期的早期预判潜在危害。尽管已有研究将人工智能偏见视为危害的来源，但生命周期中特定偏见与具体危害之间的关联仍缺乏充分理解。我们提出了ECHO——一个系统化、情境敏感且参与式的框架，它将早期危害预判锚定于生命周期偏见，并揭示这些偏见与潜在危害之间的感知关联。ECHO识别特定领域的利益相关者，通过情景案例（vignettes）实例化各类偏见，从人类参与者和大型语言模型（LLM）收集危害判断，并将这些判断组织成描述性与推断性的伦理矩阵。该框架应用于疾病诊断和招聘场景后，ECHO揭示（摘要在此处被截断）……
tldr: ECHO是一个系统化、情境敏感的参与式框架，通过将AI生命周期偏见作为危害预判的锚点，借助情景案例从利益相关者和大型语言模型收集危害判断并构建伦理矩阵，从而在AI生命周期的早期识别偏见与潜在危害之间的关联。
en_tdlr: ECHO is a systematic, context-sensitive, and participatory framework that anchors early AI harm anticipation in lifecycle biases by eliciting perceived bias-harm associations from stakeholders and an LLM through vignettes, organized into descriptive and inferential ethical matrices.
